title: Time-Bin Properties of Photon Pairs from a 2GHz Waveguide Resonator
abstract: We produce degenerate photon pairs called signal and idler via parametric down-conversion (PDC) in a Fabry-Pérot waveguide resonator having close to a 2GHz bandwidth in the telecom C-band. Our PDC source is based on a type-II periodically-poled Lithium Niobate waveguide with high-reflecting end facets forming the resonator. We measure the strength of the photon-pair correlation between signal and idler after selecting a single resonator mode from the multimode PDC emission. Thereafter, we investigate their sub-nanosecond long pulse shapes, in other words the time bins, with standard photon counting. We find that the time-bin durations vary significantly from each other, which can be predicted by the different optical losses of the cross-polarized signal and idler. Further, we simulate the temporal properties of signal and idler via the Fourier transform of their joint spectral characteristics. Our results deliver empiric insight about the time bins of photon pairs and are relevant for driving future quantum networks at the edge to narrow bandwidths but nevertheless in the pulsed regime.
summary: This paper investigates the time-bin characteristics of photon pairs generated using a PPLN waveguide resonator. By comparing measurements in multi-mode versus single-mode operation, the authors demonstrate that spectral filtering removes interference fringes and that the resulting time-bin profiles are dictated by the optical losses of the signal and idler photons. These findings are crucial for engineering pulsed quantum sources for future quantum networks.
main_problem: The study focuses on characterizing the time-bin properties of degenerate photon pairs generated via parametric down-conversion (PDC) in a waveguide resonator.
main_result: The time-bin duration varies significantly based on the optical losses of the signal and idler photons, and the presence of spectral filtering (SRM) removes interference fringes seen in the multi-mode regime (MRM).
method: The authors combine direct time-domain measurements of coincidence counts with theoretical simulations utilizing the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the Joint Spectral Intensity (JSI).
model_or_system: The physical system is a Fabry-Pérot (FP) waveguide resonator made of periodically-poled Lithium Niobate (PPLN), used as the source for degenerate photon pairs in the telecom C-band.
key_observables: Time-bin durations, Joint Spectral Intensity (JSI), Joint Temporal Intensity (JTI), and the Coincidences-to-Accidentals Ratio (CAR).
important_parameters: 2 GHz bandwidth, sub-nanosecond pulse shapes, and the Free Spectral Range (FSR) of the resonator ($\approx 6.7 	ext{ GHz}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a Gaussian pump spectrum and treats the FP Resonator classically; simulation requires choosing linear loss parameters ($\alpha$) for qualitative agreement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the JSI, spectral marginals, JTI, and measured/simulated time bins for both multi-resonator mode (MRM) and single-resonator mode (SRM) operation, showing the disappearance of interference fringes upon filtering.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using JSI and 2D Fourier transforms, then presenting experimental measurements comparing the MRM and SRM regimes, and finally analyzing the resulting time-bin characteristics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the temporal characterization of entangled photon sources, which is fundamental for developing robust quantum communication protocols and quantum networks.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Simulation in the MRM case. (a) presents the JSI in terms of the signal and idler frequencies νs,i while (b) & (c) show the spectral marginal distributions of signal and idler, respectively. (d) illustrates the 2D Fourier transform into the time domain resulting in the JTI, while (e) & (f) show the time bins of signal and idler, respectively. We have limited the frequency scales in (a) and the time scale in (b) for better visualization of the resonator modes.

(a) presents the JSI in terms of the signal and idler frequencies νs,i while (b) & (c) show the spectral marginal distributions of signal and idler, respectively. Figure 4. Linear transmission measurement for the extraordinary and ordinary crystal axis of the PPLN WG resonator together with the transmission window of the fiber coupled variable bandpass filter. The latter is applied in order to filter a SRM from the PDC emission.

Figure 5. Histogram of coincidence counts occurring between signal and idler at the pump powers of (a) 1.5 mW and (b) 3.0 mW. The counts in the central peak (red) contribute to the coincidences, while the side peaks (green) contribute to the accidentals with a black horizontal line as a guide to the eye. The spurious counts that lie outside the considered time gates are colored in blue.
